case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the Department of Human Services failed to carry its burden of showing that the Children's Records Act confidentiality provision barred release, and ordered disclosure of the aggregate number of child-abuse reports and screened-in reports from three named residential child care facilities.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion confirms that financial and operational auditing of child-welfare providers can rest on records the department must release.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that CDHS must disclose the six cardinal numbers requested by the Media Organizations.

key_cases.holding: The court held that coroners' autopsy reports are public records open to inspection under the Colorado Open Records Act, that a requester need not show a special interest to obtain them, and that a custodian who denies access must state the legal ground and may seek a protective order from the district court.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes the general CORA presumption of access that financial and program audits of public agencies depend on.
key_cases.quote: This statement of policy clearly eliminates any requirement that a person seeking access to public records show a special interest in those records in order to be permitted access thereto.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of the CORA complaint, holding that where the custodian is an individual who is also a public official the requester must first allege facts showing the record was made, maintained or kept in an official capacity before the burden shifts to the official, and that the Governor's personal cell phone bills, kept only to pay them, were not shown to be likely public records.
key_cases.relevance: Financial and program auditing through CORA reaches records made, maintained or kept in an official capacity, and this opinion draws that boundary under the current statute.
key_cases.quote: When the custodian of a requested record is an individual who is also a public official, the plaintiff must show that the record is likely a public record.
